title: Alex Ovechkin joins Wayne Gretzky as only players with 1,000 career NHL goals
content:
Alex Ovechkin took down Wayne Gretzky’s hallowed record as the greatest goal scorer in NHL history, a mark based on play in the regular season. Now he sits beside The Great One for another seemingly unapproachable goal milestone.

With his goal in the third period Sunday against the Colorado Avalanche, Ovechkin totaled 1,000 across NHL regular-season and postseason play to join Gretzky as the only players to achieve that feat.

The 40-year-old Washington Capitals superstar scored with 5:43 left in regulation on the power play in the office he has made famous, blasting a one-time shot past Avalanche goalie Mackenzie Blackwood from the left circle just above the faceoff dot. It was his 331st power-play goal, another NHL record he set long ago.

Ovechkin broke Gretzky’s previous regular-season record of 894 goals on April 6, 2025, against the New York Islanders. The winger’s 26th goal of this season on Sunday gives him 923 to go with the 77 he has scored in 161 playoff games. Gretzky has 1,016 NHL goals between the regular season and playoffs.

The Avalanche won 3-2 in overtime on Brock Nelson’s goal 1:22 into the extra period. Washington sits five points out of the Eastern Conference wild-card race with 11 games to go. Colorado boosted its lead in the Central Division to five points over the Dallas Stars, which host the Vegas Golden Knights on Sunday night.
